abstract: The mouse is a foundational model organism, yet most genomic analyses rely on linear references that fail to capture laboratory-strain genetic diversity. We present three base-level mouse pangenome graphs on the C57BL/6J telomere-to-telomere (mT2T) backbone: a 19-strain draft mouse pangenome; the founder pangenome (FP) of the 8 Collaborative Cross (CC) founders that constitute the CC's enumerable haplotype space; and the CC pangenome, the FP augmented with personalized diploid haplotypes from 40 CC recombinant inbred lines. This personalization recovers per-animal diploid genomes from short-read whole-genome sequencing at 99.2% mean concordance with expected mosaics, with substantial reproducibility in Diversity Outbred animals at very low coverage, providing a cost-effective alternative to per-sample assembly. Alignment to the FP improves both quality and accuracy of read placement compared to GRCm38 or mT2T, reducing reference-allele bias and increasing variant-calling sensitivity. The graphs support haplotype-specific analysis of methylation and allele-specific analysis of expression and chromatin accessibility.
